- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish or neutral sentiment.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is positive — cap forecast rise to 5-7% above recent peak.  
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion — if price is trending up, forecast often lags behind true breakout; adjust forecast to accelerate toward true trend by 1-2 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward momentum in bullish sentiment cycles; add 2-3% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.70 over last 5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ true values.
